newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says flights as usual.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says flights as usual.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday industrial action by its cockpit crews on the eve of salary talks would not force it to cancel flights.

"Contrary to recent claims by the Hong Kong Aircrew Officers Association (HKAOA) Cathay Pacific will not be forced to cancel flights if cockpit crew members refuse to work on guaranteed days off (G-days)," the airline said in a statement.
It said the HKAOA was about to undertake annual salary talks with Cathay Pacific, and was "falsely associating G-days with the issues of cost management and flight safety".
"Such an association is inflammatory and misleading," Cathay Pacific said.
It said a training bulge due to the introduction of new aircraft meant it had called crew members to work on G-days an average of 45 occasions a month in the past four months.
"This training bulge is now past, and fewer numbers of callouts are expected," the airline said.
Earlier, Hong Kong government radio said members of the 1,000 strong HKAOA had voted to work strictly to their contracts.
The HKAOA said management cost-cutting had left them increasingly tired, leading to cases of illness and fatigue, it reported.
